address: Gerrit Rietveld Academie, the Rietveld building (1967, Gerrit Rietveld with J. van Dillen and J. van Tricht), Fred. Roeskestraat 96: a four-storey glass box on a low dark plinth, a fully glazed curtain wall of square grey modules where every floor is a clear vision band between frosted spandrel bands, beside a low workshop wing with saw-tooth roofs
notes: Gerrit Rietveld Academie, the Rietveld building (BAG pand 0363100012077325, built 1967; 168 3DBAG wall surfaces, roof 18.2 m with stair and lift heads to 20.3 m): the four-storey glass block along the Fred. Roeskestraat canal (63 x 22 m) and the low workshop wing behind it to the south-east (saw-tooth north lights at 4.7-6.2 m).

walls[0] north front (panels 56 and 5; crops w01-357w21 2021-01-18 leaf-off at 55 m across the canal, w01-357 2019-04-30 at 25 m, w01-357s1m17/s2m17 2017-03-10): a curtain wall of square modules, 30 across the 62.9 m front, so 2.07 m (79 px at 38.1 px/m in w01-357; 19 on panel 56's 39.4 m). Every floor reads as a clear vision band about 2.1 m tall between frosted spandrel bands about 2.1 m tall (two 1.05 m panels split by a transom at the floor line): floors measured at 1.8, 6.0, 10.2 and 14.4 m and the roof at 18.5 m from the spandrel mid-rails, so a 1.8 m dark plinth (the set-back ground storey and its bicycle park) and four 4.2 m storeys; spandrels.sill and .head 0.25 of a storey each; groundFactor 0.4 (swept 0.3-0.5 against the photo mask, IoU best at 0.38-0.45). The floor line inside each merged spandrel band takes no transom (the photo shows none at that distance).

Colours hand-sampled from the crops (sample boxes in the lane report): mullions L 80-110 of 255, light grey; frosted spandrels L 70-85 (2019) and 70-76 (2021-01, against the vision glass 43-49), grey-green; vision glass dark grey-green. Chosen after the city look tints: frame #727771 (a lighter frame is lifted to cream by the city frame tint), spandrel #5e6461 (drawn as measured stone, dL 0.09 / 0.01 against the photo wall on walls[0] / walls[1]), glass #3a4240.

walls[1] west end of the north front (panel 1, surface 2, 12.5 m; crops w11-357m17 2017-03-10 and w11-357w21): a pale rendered plinth wall up to the second floor (6.0 m) under the same curtain wall; groundFactor 1.4 puts its ground storey line on walls[0]'s second floor line, palette.plinth #858880 the render (sampled #5d605a-#62645e in the overcast 2017 crop, L 95-99, lifted for exposure).

walls[2] east end of the glass block (surface 67, 20.7 m): the 2019-04-30 panorama from the Fred. Roeskestraat corner (w02-87s2far, thumbnail) shows the upper storeys' frosted and clear squares over the neighbour then standing east of it (since demolished; BAG 0363100100092566/67, building started 2025); the lower storeys are inferred as walls[0].

walls[3] south and west walls of the glass block (panels 140, 7, 14 over the workshop roof, 25): no panorama sees them (the south wall faces the courtyard between this building and the 2006 building, the west wall the 2001 neighbour); inferred as walls[0] because the block is one curtain-wall box. walls[4]: the stair and lift heads on the roof, dark grey in w01-357w21.

otherWalls: the workshop wing's walls (no panorama; the east panorama of 2019 shows the old neighbour in front of it) stay blank in the render colour of the west plinth (#858880); the narrow full-height 3DBAG slivers at the corners and the stair cores (18-21 m tall) are in walls[4] with the roof heads, dark, so no pale strips cut the glass. Not expressed: the interior columns seen through the glass, the occasional opaque infill panes in the vision bands, the bicycle racks.
roof.flatHex #818387: the PDOK orthophoto's reading of this pand (roof-facts 14/8413/5386: slot slate, rgb 132/132/132, confidence 1; roof-flat.ts), the colour the city drew it in before the install.
